# Captivate

- Category: host
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://help.captivate.fm/

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md). **Where this file and `vendors.md` differ, `vendors.md` is authoritative.**

## Integration surface

- **API:** Public REST API at `https://api.captivate.fm`, documented via a Postman collection (`docs.captivate.fm`), included with any active subscription (no sales gate). Token auth: `POST /authenticate/token` with user ID + API token to get a bearer token. Endpoints for Shows, Episodes, Media, and Analytics support both read and limited write (create/update episodes and shows, upload media/artwork). No documented rate limits were found. [Captivate API third-party profile](https://github.com/api-evangelist/captivate-fm) (third-party, 2026-09-26)
- **Webhooks:** Undocumented — no webhook/event system was found in the pages accessed this session.
- **Export formats:** RSS feed (standard, with `podcast:transcript` namespace support); CSV export of analytics (Daily Trends, How They Listen, Where They Listen, Downloads by Episode) via dashboard; API-based JSON pull of shows/episodes/media/analytics. No documented full-account bulk media export tool was found (media appears accessible per-item via the Media API). [How do I cancel a podcast?](https://help.captivate.fm/en/articles/3385348-how-do-i-cancel-a-podcast) (2026-09-26)
- **SSO / auth:** Undocumented — no SSO/SAML mention found in the help center pages accessed.
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) Dynamic/programmatic ads must be manually stripped before an outbound 301 redirect is permitted, per the cancellation flow. (2) Programmatic Ads marketplace is explicitly beta/US-only, so any ad revenue built on it is not portable or guaranteed outside the US. (3) IAB-certified analytics and download history are Captivate's own computed metrics; the docs don't describe a way to export historical per-listen raw log data, only rollup CSVs and API analytics endpoints — deeper raw-data lock-in is undocumented either way. (4) AMIE's advanced Module 2/3 (ad-server/VAST integration, marketplaces) is roadmap, not yet confirmed shipped, so relying on it prematurely would be a risk. [How do I cancel a podcast?](https://help.captivate.fm/en/articles/3385348-how-do-i-cancel-a-podcast) (2026-09-26); [How to Enable Programmatic Ads](https://help.captivate.fm/en/article/how-to-enable-programmatic-ads-ouh7ry/) (2026-09-26)

## Narrative (≤150 words)

Captivate covers Relay's core scenario cheaply: the $19/month Personal plan (plus a separately billed video add-on) already includes unlimited shows, unlimited team seats, and free private feeds, comfortably fitting 2 shows / 10k downloads / 3 seats / 1 private feed. It is a confirmed Apple HLS video launch partner and ships human-editable transcripts with `podcast:transcript` RSS support — strong on video and transcripts. Its per-show and network role systems (Viewer/Publisher/Producer/Admin, plus network-level roles) give real per-show scoping, but nothing in the docs describes an editorial approval-before-publish gate or an immutable release record — Relay would still need to build that. Comments/community are absent. Dynamic ad tooling (AMIE) is free and self-managed but true programmatic/marketplace ads are beta and US-only. The API is open to any subscriber with read/write access to shows and episodes, but webhooks and rate limits are undocumented, and outbound migration requires manually stripping dynamic ads before Captivate will set up the leaving-feed redirect.

## Research notes

- `www.captivate.fm` root-domain pages (homepage, pricing, feature-focus pages, product-release blog posts) consistently returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch in this session, likely bot protection; `help.captivate.fm` and `docs.captivate.fm`(partial) were reachable. Where a claim could only be sourced from a blocked `www.captivate.fm` page, it is marked undocumented-from-my-session or attributed to a third-party summary instead of asserted as directly verified.
- `docs.captivate.fm` (the API reference/Postman collection) returned only a bare title with no fetchable endpoint content; endpoint list is sourced from a third-party API-profile (api-evangelist GitHub repo), not Captivate's own docs directly, and should be treated as indicative, not authoritative.
- The IAB Tech Lab compliance PDF (`compliance.iabtechnologylab.com/.../07.17.2024_Captivate_-_IAB_Podcast_Measurement_Report.pdf`) was fetched but returned as binary/image content that could not be parsed for certification text in this session; certification claim (v2.2, July 2024, "first host certified") rests on Captivate's own help article plus third-party trade press (podnews.net), not a directly-read IAB registry entry. **Resolved in `vendors.md`:** the IAB Tech Lab registry web page (not the PDF) lists Captivate at v2.2, last certified 2024-07-19 `[X1]`.
- Exact private-feed/subscriber caps per plan and the exact incremental dollar cost of the Apple HLS video add-on could not be confirmed from any page I could successfully load; a search-engine-only figure ($12/month/podcast for video, and "150 subscribers per plan" for private feeds) surfaced from blocked captivate.fm pages but is NOT included as a citation since I never fetched the source page directly — flagged here instead in case it's useful to revisit with a different fetch method. **Resolved in `vendors.md`:** Captivate's help article documents the video cost as $12 per month per podcast, plus bandwidth `[CV3]`.
- No comments/community feature was found in the help center's category list; this may mean it genuinely doesn't exist, or that the category is named something not surfaced by my searches.
